content.text: The photo above shows one room before and after cleanup. Dust and scattered debris are visible on the floor in the first image; in the second, the floor is clear. It is a useful reminder that a room-by-room plan can help turn a long list of work into a manageable request.

Every home and rental is different. The comparison shows a visible change in one room, not a full project checklist. Use the ideas below to plan your own project, whether you manage a rental or are preparing a home for its next use.

Walk through the space and note what needs attention before requesting a quote. Look at floors, baseboards, windowsills, accessible fixtures and any debris. Be specific about what you want done and which rooms matter most. If something looks damaged or needs specialized work, add it to a separate list rather than assuming it is part of a basic clean.

Identify what should stay and what you want removed. For a rental, follow applicable rules and the owner's instructions before disposing of any belongings. Discuss the amount of debris and whether haul-off is included in the quote. If you encounter potentially hazardous material or a safety concern, arrange appropriate qualified help.

A clear floor is different from a repaired floor. Photos alone cannot establish the flooring material or show whether painting, repairs or specialty cleaning were performed. List scuffs, stains, damaged trim and other concerns separately, and confirm the work to be done before approving a quote.

items: Take a wide view from a similar position before and after the work so the change is easy to compare.
Add close-ups of specific conditions or concerns that matter to your checklist.
Remove or avoid personal information, mail and occupants in the frame, and get permission before sharing photos.
Keep the photos with your project notes and confirm any reporting requirements in advance.

content.text: What to Include in a Quote Request

Share the property's city, type and number of rooms or units, along with the work you need and your desired date. Mention access or scheduling constraints without posting sensitive entry details. If you have photos or a checklist, tell us and ask how to share them. Pricing and scheduling depend on the property, the agreed scope and availability.
